**Instructions.** Choose the single best answer (a–e) for each question. You may use a periodic table.
Solubility rules are **not** provided. Calculators are allowed. Answers are rounded to the precision shown.
Time yourself: aim to finish in 75 minutes or less.

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```
**1.** The reaction HCl(aq) + KOH(aq) $\rightarrow$ H~2~O(l) + KCl(aq) occurs mainly because of which driving force?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Formation of water\
b)\ Transfer of electrons\
c)\ An increase in the number of ions in solution\
d)\ Formation of a solid\
e)\ Formation of a gas

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

**5.** Which is the correct **net ionic equation** for the reaction of aqueous barium chloride with aqueous potassium sulfate?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ K^+^(aq) + Cl^−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ KCl(s)\
b)\ Ba^2+^(aq) + SO~4~^2−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ BaSO~4~(s)\
c)\ Ba^2+^(aq) + SO~4~^2−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ BaSO~4~(aq)\
d)\ Ba^2+^(aq) + 2Cl^−^(aq) + 2K^+^(aq) + SO~4~^2−^(aq) $\rightarrow$ BaSO~4~(s) + 2K^+^(aq) + 2Cl^−^(aq)\
e)\ BaCl~2~(aq) + K~2~SO~4~(aq) $\rightarrow$ BaSO~4~(s) + 2KCl(aq)

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

c)\ 8\
d)\ 11\
e)\ 12

**27.** Why must a chemical equation be balanced before it is used in a stoichiometry calculation?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ Balancing is needed only so the molar masses can be calculated\
b)\ The mole ratios used in the calculation come from the coefficients of the balanced equation\
c)\ Balancing converts the coefficients from grams into moles\
d)\ Balancing makes the total mass of the reactants equal the mass of each product\
e)\ An unbalanced equation has no limiting reactant

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```

```{=latex}
\needspace{9\baselineskip}
```

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```

b)\ the excess reactant also turns into product\

d)\ the limiting reactant is never used up\

**35.** A student reports a percent yield of 112%. Which statement is correct?

```{=latex}
\begingroup\leftskip=1.5em
```
a)\ The theoretical yield must have been calculated from the limiting reactant\
b)\ The excess reactant was converted into additional product\
c)\ Yields above 100% are normal whenever the reaction is fast\
d)\ Side reactions produced extra product beyond the theoretical yield\
e)\ Something is wrong, such as a wet or impure product or a calculation error, because the theoretical yield is the maximum possible

```{=latex}
\par\endgroup\medskip
```
